paper_metadata.title: Effect of Severe Plastic Deformation on the Structure and Properties of the Age-Hardenable Mg-Sm Alloys

evidence.section: Effect of aging on specific electrical resistance and microhardness of the Mg-4.5%Sm
evidence.quote: After SPD the Mg-4.5%Sm alloy was aged isothermally at 200 °C for up to 64 hours.
After quenching the alloys had typical structure with equiaxed gr ains of Mg solid solution.
In optical microscope, Sm-rich precipitates could be seen only after aging at 300 °C, 6h. The grain boundaries were the places of the preferable precipitation.
After aging at 200 °C, the precipitation was revealed in the electron diffraction patterns indicating the GP-zone s formation and ordering.
After aging at 300 °C, coarse plate-like precipitates were observed within grains.
SPD resulted in the formation of submicrocrystalline structure of the Mg alloys with a grain size of 100-200 nm.
The remarkable feature of the structure formed was high disl ocation density and not distinct boundaries between grains.
